language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Celestica has repeatedly reported above the top of its own guide: Q2 2026 revenue was $4.70bn against a $4.15-4.45bn guide (5.6% over the top) and adj EPS $2.54 against $2.14-2.34, and it has beaten consensus EPS 8 quarters running. TSMC, a direct upstream counterparty, reported on 2026-10-15 that Q3 revenue was $46.7bn, above its own $44.6-45.8bn guide, and said AI demand 'still exceeds supply'. A Q3 revenue print of about $5.6bn (+3% against the $5.44bn consensus, at or just over the $5.55bn top of the guide) is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells beats. Q1 2026 beat and raised, then -14.4% (2026-04-27; it had run up 60% into the print). Q4 2025 printed -13.1% (2026-01-28). Q2 2026 beat by 5.6% over the guide top, raised the year and promised faster 2027 growth, and rose +10.0% (2026-07-27), coming from 31% off the high.

findings.finding: Q3 adj EPS guidance ($2.88-3.08) was set on 2026-07-27, before the $3bn raise of 9,677,419 shares at $310 closed on about 2026-08-07/12. That adds about 8.4% to the share count, or about 5% weighted over Q3. Bernstein models $2.79 against a $2.94-3.01 consensus and says some estimates omit the dilution. A headline EPS that looks in line, or short of a stale $2.97, is plausible even if operations beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Celestica print carried a dilution mismatch. The stock fell about 13% on the raise itself (Aug 2026), so this line has moved the stock before.

findings.finding: The 2026-10-27 08:00 ET call is also Celestica's 2026 Investor and Analyst Day, so multi-year targets land inside the window. The company has already said 2027 revenue growth will exceed 65% (a floor of about $33.8bn on $20.5bn) with EPS growing faster. It is spending a $1.5bn capex placeholder for 2027, funded partly by the $3bn August raise, which is what the money buys. Bernstein models 2027 revenue at $40bn and EPS at $24.19, says the buy-side is aligned, and puts 2028 EPS at $36 against a sell-side $27. The stock has fallen about 16% since that note, so the priced 2027 bar is likely below $40bn and a target at or above it would land as a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line has decided this stock. Q2 2026 brought a raise plus 2027 acceleration: +10.0%. Q1 2026 brought a raise that fell short of lofty expectations: -14.4%. Investing.com (2026-10-26) says a solid beat may not spark a rally unless guidance is raised.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print matches the July setup that was bought, not the April setup that was sold. CLS is -24.2% over 20 days and -42.8% from its 52-week high. Three October articles attribute the fall to a sector-wide AI derating (OpenAI revenue report 10-08, Broadcom CEO's 'casino' remark 10-12, hot CPI 10-14, Anthropic's slower Q3 growth about 10-15), not to any company announcement. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-27: +60% run-in, -14.4%. 2026-07-27: 31% off the high, +10.0%. Two observations, so the relation is a lean, not a rule.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean measurement exists. CLS fell 9.8% the day after Meta's print, which suggests the hyperscaler capex line already moves this stock.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In April 2026 a raise that fell short of AI-level expectations sold off 14.4%, so the guidance-tone line is the one that has punished this name.

findings.finding: Three peers reported after Centene last spoke (07-28), and all three read positively on the lines Centene trades on. Elevance (10-21) raised 2026 guidance, said its Medicaid operating margin will land slightly ahead of its -1.75% forecast on stronger-than-expected July 1 state rate updates, and said ACA claims 'continue to develop favorably'. Molina (10-21) printed a 93.0% Medicaid MCR on 'rate updates and stable medical cost trend', a Marketplace MCR 'in line with normal seasonality', and called 'the beginning of the turn in Medicaid margins' on 2027 rates. UnitedHealth (10-13) beat and raised. Centene guided Q2 and Q3 Medicaid HBR above Q1 (93.1%) and the full year at about 93.5% (Q2 was 93.9%), so a Q3 Medicaid HBR at or below about 93.9% plus 2027 rate commentary like its peers' would sit at the good end of what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer reactions to these same signals were mixed. MOH fell about 8.5% intraday on 10-21 despite a beat and a reaffirmed guide (goldesel.de, 2026-10-21); UNH gained about 3% (XTB, 2026-10-13). Centene's own Medicaid-HBR beats: Q1 2026 +13.95%, Q2 2026 -0.27%.

findings.finding: The Q3 bar is set unusually low by Centene itself ('a little above breakeven'; consensus about $0.07-0.09), and in 2026 the company has run well ahead of its own expectations. Q1 adjusted EPS of $3.37 was 'about $0.50 above the company's expectations'; Q2 was $2.51 against about $1.02 consensus (about $0.50 of it was non-recurring 2025 settlements). The FY floor went from >$3.40 to >$4.80 in one quarter. H1 adjusted EPS is $5.88, so the >$4.80 floor implies an H2 loss of about $1.08, against consensus about -$0.99. Any Q3 print above about $0.10 lifts the FY floor mechanically, unless Q4 is guided down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a $1.49 EPS beat and floor raised from >$3.40 to >$4.80, stock -0.27%. Q1 2026: a $0.50 beat and raise, +13.95%. Q3 2025: +12.5%. Beat-and-raise has paid on 2 of the last 3 prints, and the largest beat bought nothing.

findings.finding: Management said it will give 'a better viewpoint' on 2027 on this Q3 call. The bridge is hard on Centene's own words. About $0.50 of 2026 EPS is 2025 settlements that 'would not recur in 2027'. OB3 Medicaid expansion attrition is 'mid-single digit' over 2027-2029. Rate lag 'mutes' margin recovery through H2 2026 and part of 2027, with acceleration only 'late 2027'. Centene is exiting New Hampshire ACA and Arkansas ARHOME (about 77k members). FY2027 consensus is $5.34 (range $4.99-6.25) against an FY2026 consensus of $4.89; ex the $0.50 non-recurring that base is about $4.39, so the street needs about 22% underlying growth. An early 2027 framing below about $5 is a guidance miss on the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-look outlooks have moved this name the most: 2025-07-01 guidance withdrawal -40.37%, and Q4 2025 (02-05, 2026 guide) -3.66%. Q3 2025 commentary (10-28-2025) +12.5%.

findings.finding: CMS said on 2026-09-22 it would cancel about 315,000 Marketplace enrollments covering more than 760,000 people as improper, recoup the associated subsidies, and freeze new agent/broker registration for plan year 2027. Centene is the largest on-exchange carrier (about 3.5M Marketplace members at 06-30), so a share of the cancellations, a subsidy clawback, or a reserve could land in Q3 or the 2026 Marketplace margin (guided 4.5-5%). Oscar flagged 250-300k of its own members in August and said the effect was in its guidance; Centene has disclosed no number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marketplace was the line behind the 2025-07-01 -40.37% (risk-adjustment shock). Q2 2026's Marketplace favourability came with a flat reaction (-0.27%).

findings.finding: The 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings released by CMS on 10-08 (they set 2028 quality bonuses) cut Centene's share of members in 4+ star plans from 18% to 9% (Stephens, via Becker's). Centene's unweighted average fell from 3.31 to 3.14, and five Wellcare contracts are at 2.5 stars or below. Capstone called it likely neutral for Centene. The call may quantify the 2028 bonus loss inside a Medicare segment that management targets at 'break even or better' for 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stars updates have moved CNC before (Bloomberg Government: 'Centene Surges on ... Star Scores Update', https://news.bgov.com/insurance/centene-surges-on-positive-view-of-early-medicare-quality-scores). The stock has looked through this one so far, rising after 10-08.

findings.finding: Ambetter announced on 10-20 that it is expanding into 55 more counties for plan year 2027, while keeping about 3.5M members across 27 states. Management had said on 07-28 that it would 'get visibility into our competitive positioning as we get into Q3', so expanding after seeing competitors' filed rates suggests it is comfortable with 2027 Marketplace pricing and margin. This comes on top of large requested increases (Ambetter about +40% average in Pennsylvania).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marketplace margin restoration drove the Q1 2026 +13.95% (Marketplace HBR 75.3%) and the guide raise to 4.5-5% margin in Q2 (-0.27%).

findings.finding: Centene redeemed all of its remaining $568.7M of 4.25% notes due December 2027 on 2026-10-23, from cash and ahead of the print. That clears a 2027 maturity and is consistent with the strong statutory and parent cash that its 2026 raises imply. It is a modest positive or a zero.

findings.finding: The Q3 rate shock on SoFi's fair-value loan book was about 2.5 times Q2's. On the Treasury par curve, June 30 to September 30, 2026: 2y 4.14% to 4.88% (+74bp), 3y 4.15% to 5.00% (+85bp), 5y 4.19% to 5.09% (+90bp). In Q2 the same tenors rose 27-35bp (March 31: 3.79/3.81/3.92) and personal-loan marks still fell 71bp to 104.7%. About $46.7B of loans are carried at fair value (10-Q, June 30, 2026), so the Q3 mark-down before hedges is plausibly several hundred million dollars, against a quarterly adjusted net revenue bar of about $1.25B. Hedge offsets are not disclosed in anything I could read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 and Q2 2026 both carried rate-driven mark-downs (Q1 benchmark +31bp, Q2 personal-loan marks -71bp) and both still beat revenue (Q2 $1.21B against $1.11B). The stock fell 15.4% after Q1 and 8.9% after Q2 on guidance and profit, not on the marks themselves.

findings.finding: The unchanged FY2026 guide of about $825M adjusted net income and about $0.60 adjusted EPS needs a steep second half. H1 adjusted net income was $327.1M ($0.24 a share; Q2 $160.4M, $0.12), so H2 needs about $498M, or about $0.18 a quarter, which is 50% above Q2's run-rate. Q3 consensus of $0.17 already assumes most of that ramp. The guide was set assuming one or two Fed hikes, and Q3 delivered a September hike plus an 85bp shift in the 3-5y part of the curve. Holding $0.60 is a stretch; cutting it repeats the April and July pattern (EPS guide not raised, stock down).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 29, 2026: revenue guide raised to $4.75-4.85B with EBITDA and EPS held, and the stock fell 8.9% (baseline; Reuters via TIKR blamed the unchanged profit outlook). April 29, 2026: the stock fell 15.4% on guidance described as underwhelming despite a revenue beat.

findings.finding: Rates retraced in October, which gives management room to hold the Q4 and FY guide. By October 23 the par curve was 2y 4.69% (from 4.88% on Sep 30), 3y 4.75% (from 5.00%), 5y 4.82% (from 5.09%) and 10y 5.00% (from 5.29%), so quarter-to-date marks have partly recovered. SoFi can cite this on the call as support for Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent in the baseline. In 2025, when rates eased, prints were rewarded (+6.6% Jul-25, +5.5% Oct-25).

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 revenue should land around $7.6-8.0M against the single-analyst bar of $7.25M (+5-10%). The base is Q4 FY25 revenue of $7.5M (ad $5.2M, subscription $1.4M). Subscription revenue has grown 31-32% a year, recognised from a deferred-revenue balance of $6.2M (+26%). Marketplace ad revenue is flat on higher prices per impression. Against that, Emojipedia ad revenue fell 53%. The same analyst's Q3 bar was $7.0M and the print was $7.99M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-06-11): a 14% revenue beat against the same $7.0M bar bought +25.7% close to close, then gave almost all of it back the next session (4.16 to 3.25, per the Yahoo daily bars). Q4 FY25 (2025-10-28): flat revenue with restructuring fell -24.3%. Q2 FY26: revenue +18% with an Emojipedia impairment fell -14.5%.

findings.finding: This is the first fiscal-year-end call under new CEO Morris Berger (from 2026-10-01). He is on $450k salary plus options on 3% of shares, and the strategy has moved to building DataSeeds.AI into a core business: talent, technology, datasets and selective acquisitions, funded by the $7.675M insider placement, with the buyback suspended. The company guided to 'improved profitability and FCF' for FY26 a year ago. Any FY27 framing is now likely to be an investment year with higher opex, which works against the ~20% FCF-yield valuation case. The size of the spend has not been disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last fiscal-year-end print with forward framing (Q4 FY25, 2025-10-28) fell -24.3%. The Aug 31 pivot announcement itself traded +5.9% (2.87 to 3.04 on 949k shares) and then drifted back below $2.90.

findings.finding: The Q3 FY26 10-Q shows subscription billings down 4.4% to $1,757K while recognised subscription revenue rose 31.9% to $1,678K. Developed-market MAU fell 17.3% to 4.3M, and those are the higher-priced subscribers. The 30%+ subscription revenue growth the release headlines is coming off deferred lifetime-subscription revenue while new billings shrink, so the growth line should decelerate. The FY 10-K and call will expose that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction is attributable to billings. MAU declines have run at -11% for several quarters (Q4 FY25 -11.1%, Q3 FY26 -11.3%) through both +25.7% and -24.3% reactions, so the market has not reliably punished MAU.

findings.finding: Insiders put $7.675M into Class B stock at $2.93-2.98 (closed 2026-09-25). Howard Jonas's Chartwell alone put in $6.5M, unborrowed, taking him to 15.6%. The stock is now $2.71, with pro-forma cash of $27.4M (~$1.75/share on ~15.7M shares) and no debt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line. The placement close (2026-09-25 to 09-30) coincided with a drift from 3.09 to 2.88.

findings.finding: The fiscal-year-end impairment test is the risk window. Remaining goodwill is $2.14M and net intangibles $1.07M at 2026-04-30. GuruShots monthly active payers fell 37.7% and Emojipedia revenue fell 53% after a $3.7M impairment in Q2. Any Q4 non-cash charge is capped at about $3M, roughly 7% of market cap, below operating income, with no path to the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FY26 print that carried the $3.7M Emojipedia impairment fell -14.5%, together with an EPS miss.

findings.finding: DataSeeds signed its first six-figure model-evaluation contract (reported 2026-09-01) and completed its first commercial evals engagement for Bria.AI (press release 2026-10-19). Neither has a revenue figure. The new CEO's first call will likely use these as pipeline evidence, and they mostly fall into Q1 FY27 revenue rather than Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 FY26 print that announced DataSeeds' first six-figure order rose +25.7%. The Bria release on 2026-10-19 moved the stock 2.78 to 2.79, which is nothing.

outside_window.finding: The placement warrants (2.35M shares at $3.22/$3.28) become exercisable only after stockholder approval and March 2027. They add dilution and an overhang above the current price, but nothing exercisable inside the window.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 EPS carries the second semi-annual coupon on the $200M 7.50% AT1 notes issued in September 2025 (about $7.5M, ~$0.20 a share). This is the first Q3 to carry it. Q1 2026 EPS was $1.31 on $56.4M of net profit ($1.54 before the coupon), and the company says Q1 EPS 'reflect[s] the deduction of the AT1 coupon distribution'. Q2 EPS was $1.77 on $66.5M. If aggregator estimates run Q2's $1.77 forward, headline EPS will print well below them even with flat net profit. Year-ago Q3 2025 EPS was $1.48 with no coupon.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 was the first print with the coupon (EPS -13% q/q, -7% y/y, released 2026-04-27 amc). I could not find its next-day reaction. The baseline's reaction history is cadence-implausible; the only confirmed earnings reaction in it is Q2 2026 (2026-07-27 amc), +1.08%.

findings.finding: Q2 fees and non-interest income ($25.6M, +86% q/q, with $7.9M of upfront structuring and syndication fees from a record 7 deals) were flagged as exceptional. The CEO said 'I do not advise to simply multiply for the rest of the year because of the syndication part'. A Q3 fee line nearer the $13-20M range would take net profit below Q2's $66.5M record.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's record fee quarter bought +1.08% (baseline, 2026-07-27 amc). No sourced reaction to a fee shortfall quarter.

findings.finding: The commercial portfolio was already up 17% since year-end at June 30 ($13.0B, +8% q/q) against a full-year guide of 13-15% growth. Asked why the guide was not raised, the CEO said 'there might be upside in our guidance of loan growth, but we're not ready to say that yet' and that they were 'retaining the guidance until we have better visibility on the second half'. Q3 is the natural point to raise it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced prior guidance-raise reaction for BLX. The Q2 reaffirmation with record results bought +1.08%.

findings.finding: The Fed raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. On the Q2 call the CEO had expected rates 'to remain stable for longer'. Bladex's book is ~65-70% due within 12 months and largely floating, so it reprices quickly. The hike lands only in the last two weeks of Q3, but it supports the ~2.30% NIM guide (1H 2.29%, Q2 2.24% and falling) and the Q4 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced BLX reaction to a NIM-guide change. Q2's 10bp NIM decline came with a +1.08% reaction.

findings.finding: Q2 Stage 3 rose to $75M (0.5%) from migrating 'a single client in the petrochemical sector in Brazil'. Bladex sold the bilateral loan but kept a reserved deferred-payment letter of credit, and reserve coverage fell to 1.25x. Management targets 1.5-1.6x by year-end, which requires a reserve build. Braskem, which fits that description, was cut to RD by Fitch on 2026-08-14 and filed for extrajudicial recovery on 2026-08-24 on about US$10.9B of unsecured debt. The plan offers no principal haircut, five extra years and 30 months without interest, so a further specific provision on the residual LC is possible in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 carried the first Stage 3 migration and provisions doubled to $8.6M, and the stock still rose +1.08%, so this name's holders have looked through a single-name migration once.

findings.finding: Q2 portfolio growth was led by Panama and Argentina (Argentine exposure mainly oil and gas and short-term gas imports). From August to October Argentine sovereign dollar bonds were the worst emerging-market performers: yields near 12%, spreads at their widest in more than a year, and the Merval down more than 10% in September. This risks Stage 2 migration, a Stage 1 provision build or a defensive call tone on a newly enlarged country exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced BLX reaction to a country-risk provision.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-08 Bladex placed MXN 5.0B of three-year Cebures at TIIE de Fondeo +58bp, 1.56x covered and rated AAA local by S&P and Fitch. This is funding for a portfolio growing 20% y/y, not distress: the money buys balance-sheet growth that the Q2 numbers corroborate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction. The April 2026 Cebures (MXN 4.27B) preceded a record Q2.

findings.finding: Management guided expenses up in the second half ('expense execution is seasonally weighted towards the second half') and the efficiency ratio to 27-28% for the year, against 24.1% in Q2 and 25.2% in 1H. That implies a step-up in Q3/Q4 opex from Q2's $23.8M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction. Opex +14% y/y in Q2 came with a +1.08% reaction.

outside_window.finding: Braskem Chapter 15 recognition hearing scheduled to run to 2026-12-08. Creditor treatment of bank LC exposure is not final before then.
Next FOMC decision 2026-10-28, after the exit window closes on 2026-10-27; a further hike would add to NIM tailwind in Q4.
